question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{-5x+2y}{x}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{-5x+2(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=-5+2v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=-5+v \\ \frac{1}{-5+v}\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\frac{1}{-5+v}\,\mathrm{d}v&=\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \ln|v-5|&=\ln|x|+C_1 \\ |v-5|&=e^{C_1}|x| \\ v-5&=Cx \\ v&=Cx+5\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x}&=Cx+5 \\ y&=Cx^2+5x\end{aligned}
$$

The signed constant $C$ absorbs $e^{C_1}$. Division by $v-5$ excluded $v=+5$; restoring it permits $C=0$, giving $y=+5x$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{-8x+y}{x}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{-8x+(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=-8+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=-8 \\ \frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{-8}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\mathrm{d}v&=-8\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ v&=-8\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x}&=-8\ln|x|+C \\ y&=-8x\ln|x|+Cx\end{aligned}
$$



The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{6x^3+y^3}{xy^2}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{6x^3+(vx)^3}{x(vx)^2} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{6+v^3}{v^2}=\frac{6}{v^2}+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{6}{v^2} \\ v^2\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{6}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int v^2\,\mathrm{d}v&=6\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \frac{v^3}{3}&=6\ln|x|+C_1 \\ v^3&=18\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^3&=18\ln|x|+C \\ y^3&=x^3(18\ln|x|+C) \\ y&=x\sqrt[3]{18\ln|x|+C}\end{aligned}
$$

Here $C=3C_1$ and the cube root is real. Restrict the solution to intervals where $y\ne0$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{-3x^3+y^3}{xy^2}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{-3x^3+(vx)^3}{x(vx)^2} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{-3+v^3}{v^2}=\frac{-3}{v^2}+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{-3}{v^2} \\ v^2\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{-3}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int v^2\,\mathrm{d}v&=-3\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \frac{v^3}{3}&=-3\ln|x|+C_1 \\ v^3&=-9\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^3&=-9\ln|x|+C \\ y^3&=x^3(-9\ln|x|+C) \\ y&=x\sqrt[3]{-9\ln|x|+C}\end{aligned}
$$

Here $C=3C_1$ and the cube root is real. Restrict the solution to intervals where $y\ne0$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$.

\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{9x+y}{x}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{9x+(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=9+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=9 \\ \frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{9}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\mathrm{d}v&=9\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ v&=9\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x}&=9\ln|x|+C \\ y&=9x\ln|x|+Cx\end{aligned}
$$
